seo.og_description: Explore Rabat: Udayas kasbah, Hassan Tower, Chellah ruins, medina lanes and the Bouregreg estuary on the Atlantic.

name: Rabat
hero_subtitle: Morocco’s capital on the Atlantic — kasbah cliffs, Hassan Tower, Chellah and a calm Bouregreg waterfront.

overview.title: A capital that still feels walkable
overview.p1: Rabat sits where the Bouregreg meets the Atlantic: the white-and-blue Kasbah of the Udayas above the river mouth, the unfinished Hassan Tower and Mohammed V Mausoleum, the Roman-Islamic ruins of Chellah, and a medina that stays manageable compared with Fez or Marrakech. As the political capital it is ordered and green, yet the ocean wind and estuary light keep it from feeling purely administrative.
overview.p2: Two or three days cover the kasbah, Hassan complex, Chellah, medina and a walk along the marina or beach. Day trips reach Salé across the river, or further to Casablanca and the coast toward Kenitra. Base yourself near the medina, Hassan district or Agdal depending on whether you prefer historic lanes or modern cafés.

places.title: Must-visit places in Rabat
places.subtitle: Kasbah, tower, necropolis, medina and the Bouregreg shore.

oudayas.title: Kasbah of the Udayas
oudayas.desc: White-and-blue quarter above the river mouth with Andalusian gardens.

hassan.title: Hassan Tower
hassan.desc: Iconic Almohad minaret and the esplanade of the unfinished mosque.

mausoleum.title: Mohammed V Mausoleum
mausoleum.desc: Marble and zellige memorial beside Hassan Tower.

chellah.title: Chellah
chellah.desc: Roman and Merinid necropolis in a walled garden by the Bouregreg.

medina.title: Rabat Medina
medina.desc: Compact lanes, souks and the Andalusian wall near the ocean.

gardens.title: Andalusian Gardens
gardens.desc: Shaded gardens inside the Udayas kasbah.

marina.title: Bouregreg Marina
marina.desc: Modern marina and promenade facing Salé across the estuary.

beach.title: Rabat Beach
beach.desc: Atlantic sand below the walls and along the corniche.

museum.title: Museums of Rabat
museum.desc: Archaeology and modern collections in the capital.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-day itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Kasbah and Hassan first, then Chellah and the waterfront.

detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Kasbah of the Udayas & Andalusian Gardens — views over the Bouregreg and Atlantic.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Medina lanes, Rue des Consuls and a café stop near the ocean walls.
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Sunset from the kasbah platform or a quiet dinner in the medina (Dinarjat, Dar Naji).
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Hassan Tower esplanade and Mohammed V Mausoleum — allow time for security checks.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Chellah ruins and gardens; storks on the walls in season.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Bouregreg marina promenade or a rooftop near Hassan / Agdal.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Museum stop or ferry/walk toward Salé’s medina across the river.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Rabat beach or corniche walk; free time in Agdal cafés if you prefer the modern city.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Last mint tea in the Udayas or dinner facing the estuary.

directory.title: Find Your Ideal Stay in Rabat
directory.subtitle: Medina riads, Hassan hotels and Agdal apartments — filter by type and area.

eat.title: Where to eat in Rabat
eat.subtitle: Medina houses, kasbah cafés and modern tables in Agdal and Hassan.

dinarjat.title: Le Dinarjat
dinarjat.desc: Traditional Moroccan in a restored house — booking advised.

naji.title: Dar Naji
naji.desc: Reliable tagines and salads in a lively medina setting.

imprevu.title: L'Imprévu
imprevu.desc: Contemporary cooking popular with locals and diplomats.

maure.title: Café Maure
maure.desc: Mint tea and pastries with river views inside the kasbah.

goeland.title: Le Goéland
goeland.desc: Seafood and Atlantic catch when you want fish.

tour.title: Restaurant de la Tour Hassan
tour.desc: Hotel restaurant near the tower — convenient after sightseeing.

food.title: Eating in the capital
food.p1: Rabat’s food scene mixes medina houses, simple grills and a growing list of modern restaurants in Hassan and Agdal. Seafood follows the Atlantic; tagines and salads stay central to everyday meals.
food.li1: Book Le Dinarjat for a classic medina dinner.
food.li2: Café Maure for tea with a view in the Udayas.
food.li3: Agdal and Hassan for international and contemporary menus.
food.li4: Fresh juice and pastries along Avenue Mohammed V.
food.li5: Salé across the river for a different local lunch scene.

1.title: Getting around
1.desc: Tram links Rabat and Salé; taxis are plentiful. The historic core is walkable between Udayas, medina and Hassan.

2.title: Dress & visits
2.desc: Modest dress helps at the mausoleum; security checks are normal at official sites.

3.title: Wind & weather
3.desc: Atlantic wind can be cool even in sun — a light layer helps on the kasbah terrace.

daytrips.title: Day trips from Rabat
daytrips.subtitle: Across the Bouregreg or further along the coast and inland.

sale.title: Salé
sale.desc: Medina and beach just across the Bouregreg — tram or boat.

casa.title: Casablanca
casa.desc: About 1 hour by train — Hassan II Mosque and corniche.

kenitra.title: Kenitra & Mehdia
kenitra.desc: Coast and lagoon north of the capital.

meknes.title: Meknes & Volubilis
meknes.desc: Longer day — imperial city and Roman ruins inland.

q1.question: How many days in Rabat?
q1.answer: Two full days cover the main sites; three let you add Salé, museums or a slower beach afternoon.

q2.question: Is Rabat worth visiting vs Marrakech?
q2.answer: Yes if you want a calmer capital with ocean air, major monuments and fewer souk crowds.

q3.question: Airport code?
q3.answer: RBA (Rabat-Salé). Casablanca CMN is an alternative with more flights, then train to Rabat.

q4.question: Safe for walking?
q4.answer: The main tourist areas are generally fine by day; use normal city awareness at night.

q5.question: Best area to stay?
q5.answer: Medina/Udayas for atmosphere, Hassan for monuments, Agdal for modern cafés and space.
